read_this_first: Thresholds are data, not code: change a number here and scripts/windows_check.py and win/step0_pc_tests.ps1 follow. Every block has a source. (J) marks a proposal by the planner that has no external source; the orchestrator or the maker may change it. Windows behaviour behind these fields is UNVERIFIED until the maker's first real report.

gpu.software_name_patterns_source: Names that mean no real graphics card: .claude/skills/ai-photo-to-animation-pipeline/SKILL.md step 2 (llvmpipe, SwiftShader, Basic Render count as no GPU); the remote, Hyper-V and WARP entries are the planner's additions (J).

tiers.meaning: 16 GB or more: adds Qwen-Image-Edit-2511 and PuLID-FLUX
8 to 15 GB: Real-ESRGAN, CodeFormer, smaller SeedVR2 builds, FLUX.2 klein 4B, FramePack, WanGP
a real graphics device under 8 GB: CPU-first path, small tools only

gpu.tiers_source: playbooks/ai-imagery.md Decision 2 (No GPU / 8 to 12 GB Nvidia / 16 GB or more). The cut-offs sit half a gigabyte below the round numbers (7.5 and 15.5) because cards report a little under their name (an 8 GB card often shows 8187 MiB, a 16 GB card 16376 MiB) (J).
gpu.non_nvidia_source: playbooks/ai-imagery.md names the 8 to 12 GB tier as Nvidia and the listed tools (FramePack, Real-ESRGAN CUDA builds, Qwen, PuLID) assume CUDA. A non-NVIDIA card is therefore capped at gpu-low until a test says otherwise (J). Set this to null to turn the cap off.
gpu.vram_sources_trusted_source: F-11 in build/BUILD-PLAN-W1-2.md: Win32_VideoController.AdapterRAM is a 32-bit field that caps near 4 GB (UNVERIFIED on the maker's PC). It is trusted only when it is below the cap (an integrated device), never when flagged adapterram_capped_4gb.
gpu.adapterram_cap_source: A value at or above 0xFFF00000 (4,293,918,720) is the 32-bit ceiling; 4,294,967,295 is the other common ceiling (general knowledge, UNVERIFIED on the maker's PC).

vram_buckets.source: Coarse buckets for the filed tier file so no exact size is stored (build plan 4.16). Edges are the planner's choice (J); they use the same half-gigabyte tolerance as the tiers (7.5, 11.5, 15.5, 23.5 are applied before bucketing).

tiers.meaning: WSL2 fits (default cap is half of RAM); Craft apps and a VM can run together
meets the Blender floor; WSL2 not advised: one heavy program at a time
below the Blender 5 floor of 8 GB

ram.tiers_source: Blender floor of 8 GB: research/toolchain.md item 15 and [30]. WSL2 at 16 GB or more: research/toolchain.md F3 (the WSL2 VM gets 50 percent of Windows RAM by default). Windows reports 16 GB as about 15.7 to 16.0 and 8 GB as about 7.4 to 7.9, so the cut-offs are 15.0 and 7.5 (J).

blender_floor.source: research/toolchain.md item 15 and F3: Blender 5.x needs at least 4 cores, 8 GB RAM and a 2 GB VRAM GPU with OpenGL 4.3 or Vulkan 1.3 [30]. Printed as information; below the floor is a fact about the PC, not a failure.

tiers.meaning: archive, masters, scans and renders all fit without cleaning
fits if renders are cleaned as you go
plan an external drive for the archive and masters

disk.source: (J) planner's proposal. A 12-minute ProRes 422 HQ 1080p24 master is roughly 16 GB (about 176 Mbit/s: general knowledge, UNVERIFIED here); 400 prints scanned at 600 ppi are roughly 40 GB (research/ai-imagery.md); working copies and renders double it. Judged on the fixed or removable drive with the most free space.

edition.source: BitLocker drive encryption is offered on Windows Pro and higher; Home editions have only device encryption (Microsoft documentation, general knowledge, UNVERIFIED here). A VeraCrypt file container works on every edition (DECISIONS.md W-25). EditionID values: Core and CoreSingleLanguage are Home; Professional is Pro.

display.source: (J) planner's classes by the primary screen's pixel width. The film is mastered at 1920x1080 (settings card), so below-fhd cannot show a full-size preview.

python.source: playbooks/agent-pipeline.md Step 2 names Python 3.13 (winget Python.Python.3.13). The repo's Windows-side tools use only the standard library; 3.10 is the planner's minimum (J).

ffmpeg.source: The container tests used ffmpeg 6.1.1; playbooks/agent-pipeline.md Step 2 names the winget build Gyan.FFmpeg 9.0.2, which is not the container build, so the colour-patch test must be run on whichever build is on the PC. libx264 is needed for the venue and phone H.264 files and libass for burned-in captions (theatrical-delivery notes); zscale is optional because the frozen chains do not use it (build plan 4.5). The 6.x floor is the planner's choice (J).

accounts.source: O-03 in DECISIONS.md asks whether she shares the PC. Two or more enabled local accounts is only a hint (J): the answer is about her home, not the machine, so it is printed in the chat table and never filed.
